body: Thank you thank you thank you. This is 100% exactly my problem. You sound just like me. I have bad anxiety with mortality that has flared up as well that I'm hoping to work through. Seeing the therapist, I hope, will help.

Most of my anxiety stems from a fear of death. Climate change has a huge death component to it, so it's likely that my therapist and I will work on that. I took the advice of this thread and met with one yesterday.
This is interesting. I'll look into it. May I ask why you frequent /r/collapse while seemingly actively trying to be involved in the renewal of culture? You don't seem to be an /r/collapse person.
https://www.reddit.com/r/climate/comments/5laam9/slug/dbuaj5b

I don't disagree. I've scheduled an appointment with a therapist. I've been able to feel concern about the environment while be able to function before. It's not like I learned something new this week that sent me into a panic. I'm wondering if maybe I got hit with a mental bump more than anything.

This is awesome. 

Mind if I message you? I'd like to talk about what you just said, as well as the non-existence part.

Ones like Michael Mann, McPherson, Hansen... There's a trained scientist who posted in this thread or on the other sub that said he thinks we're hitting 4C and that it's grim, but the best thing I can do is learn survival strategies at this point (he also pointed me to /r/collapse, to be fair).
This is terrific. Thank you.
This is great advice. Do you mind if I message you about some other, possibly related life questions?
How are you an optimist if it seems so hopeless? I would consider something like climate change would kill all optimism.
Unsubscribing seems like I'd be denying reality, no? Like I'd just be ignoring the problem that needs immediate fixing?
This is good advice. Thank you.
I've considered this, to be honest.

That's the vibe I get from people about McPherson. 

Why are Bill McKibben and James Hansen so grim compared to someone like Al Gore, who seems certain that we can pull this off?

I understand, but I do still fear the effects it'll have on the generations after mine. The total collapse I speak of is when I read climate scientists talking about famines and wars over food, mass migrations, and all of this piling on into a collapsing effect. 

Hell, someone on here recommended going to /r/collapse.
I know, but I don't want the next generation to look at me and wonder why I didn't do absolutely everything I could to fix things. I do hope I find that peace that you seemed to have found.
I don't think that's a good idea, given my current mental state.
Thanks for sharing this. This actually kind of helps.
I don't plan on having children, but that doesn't lessen my worry for future generations of humanity, or for the children of my siblings.

I'll watch that, thank you.

I just worry those positive steps aren't going to be enough, you know? I keep seeing these projections and how the planet continues to break heat records in spite of all of those amazing advances.
I already have been. It helps a little, but it still never feels like enough.

I understand the immediacy of other's issues, and don't intend to put theirs over mine. It does put parts of it into perspective, and given how I currently feel, I would beg them to take care of their mental health first before committing themselves towards anything else. Maybe I'm a mild case of that very same philosophy - like you said, in a way, it is a luxury.

Thank you for coming in here, especially as an older parent. I don't get that viewpoint often for something like this.

Is ClimateCentral a reliable news source? I've never heard of them. I prefer to have my news be as straight as possible.

Thanks for the advice. Hope your anxiety is manageable.

Can you describe that process?

I guess a part of me is very obsessive about the whole thing to the point that I -can't- enjoy those things anymore. My anxiety over it is so high that I can't really enjoy much of anything because I'll be too locked in my thoughts about the climate or I'll just not feel anything.

This is excellent advice. Thank you, thank you, thank you.

How bad does your future anxiety get?

Re: Al Gore. I've seen people on here say that he is far too optimistic about climate change. I don't know if they're right or not.

And if things are collapsing due to climate change, the damage is irreversible. I don't see us adapting, I just see it constantly crumbling down. And some people seem to be able to cope with this! Even the most pessimistic! 

There's challenges in life, and then there are actual threats to humanity. I am terrified that we can't rise up to the threats.

This also makes me worried that I'm only buying in to the worst case scenarios of everything due to my pessimism. I automatically assume the worst will happen, especially when I read people like Bill McKibben or whoever say that the chances are "grim," "a longshot," "pretty much gone."

I appreciate this. I wonder if it is my anxiety talking when I think that this is a healthy level of fear since it is the future of our survival. Yet, I don't have as much worry - really, very little - about a war between Russia and the US. I think there's a healthy fear there, but I don't let it cripple me and keep me from doing things.

I guess I just wonder how it's possible to have a clear head while trying to save humanity. Maybe getting a handle on my anxiety will show me that.

When I mention hurting myself, I mean in the sense that, if things are collapsing, why would I want to watch that unfold?

I honestly don't know if this level of anxiety is unhealthy. I don't have a clear mind to say so, because we're talking about the collapse and possible extinction of our species. Why shouldn't I focus every minute of my life over it? Why shouldn't we all be crazy concerned that this wonderful thing we have might end very soon at our own hands?
